research_basis.use: 405 applies to a known target resource with unsupported method and requires Allow; 201 is the semantic create response and Location is recommended when a resource is created.
Pydantic request validation can produce 422; response_model validates/documents/filters output and is represented in OpenAPI.
Standard members include type/title/status/detail/instance; trace_id is an extension, not a standard member; media type is application/problem+json.
Idempotency-Key remains a draft rather than an RFC; reuse with a different payload is prohibited and resource-specific fingerprint/scope/expiry semantics matter.
I/O-bound async, CPU-bound parallelism, and durable work are distinct; heavy/durable work generally requires a separate worker/queue rather than process-local BackgroundTasks.
429 represents too many requests in a given amount of time and may carry a Retry-After header.

research_basis.source: Zalando RESTful API Guidelines / Microsoft API Guidelines
research_basis.use: Backward compatibility includes types, requiredness, enum evolution, error contracts, semantics, ordering/pagination and operational behavior, not merely preserving field names.

runtime_counterexamples.impact: Unknown path is mislabeled Method Not Allowed although the lesson itself says unknown path is 404.
Invalid page size crashes rather than failing contract validation.
Negative page size silently creates nonsensical pagination.
Unknown cursor is silently treated as end-of-data, masking stale/tampered cursors.
Duplicate/non-unique cursor values make continuation ambiguous.

runtime_counterexamples.case: Store mutable request body by reference, mutate original body, then replay new value
runtime_counterexamples.impact: The supposed original request fingerprint changes after insertion; no canonical immutable snapshot exists.
Presence-only validator accepts wrong types despite prose promising type/range validation.
Canonical code contradicts the paragraph that durable work must leave the request and be durably queued.
Impossible negative elapsed time passes the timeout contract.
Ordered negative budgets pass the cascade gate.
Impossible test counts satisfy the supposed pyramid-quality gate.
Negative usage produces more remaining quota than the configured limit.
PII embedded in values passes the privacy gate because only top-level key names are checked.
Case/alias variation passes the exact-name ban list.

rejected_findings.claim: FastAPI using 422 for request validation is wrong.
rejected_findings.evidence: FastAPI officially uses RequestValidationError/422 for validation failures; the defect is that S41's own executable checks only field presence.

rejected_findings.claim: Keyset pagination is inherently inferior to offset.
rejected_findings.evidence: Keyset pagination is a valid and often more stable choice; S41's defect is lack of a unique immutable ordering/cursor contract and invalid-cursor handling.
RFC 9457 permits extension members; the defect is calling trace_id part of the RFC's standard member set.
They are valid for small process-local post-response work; the defect is using one 'background' label for CPU isolation and durable work while the executable queue is an in-memory list.

rejected_findings.claim: Current PDF still labels S41 FineTune.
rejected_findings.evidence: Current PdfReport.tsx maps llm-finetuning to '41. API FastAPI'.

rejected_findings.claim: REST APIs are required by HTTP to use noun-only paths.
rejected_findings.evidence: Noun-oriented resources are a useful API design convention, not an HTTP protocol requirement; recorded instead as S41-F40 wording overreach.

findings.summary: S41 starts Phase 3 while S39/CF-3 and S40 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: Authoritative continuation explicitly keeps S39/CF-3 and S40 debt active.
findings.attack: A clean HTTP facade can launder stale ER/graph/model/policy evidence into an apparently governed service.
findings.defense: Building an API after architecture is the correct curricular order.
findings.fix: Make upstream artifact/version/hash and gate status explicit preconditions of every S41 service example.

findings.summary: S41 repeatedly calls its local gate CP-N4-A even though the authoritative roadmap places CP-N4-A at S43.
findings.evidence: Roadmap capstone table: CP-N4-A gate S43; S41 callout says 'CP-N4-A se demuestra con evidencia local'.
findings.attack: Learner can believe the capstone is promoted two sections early, before S42 security/privacy and S43 deployment/contract work.
findings.defense: S41 legitimately contributes an increment toward CP-N4-A.
findings.fix: Call S41 an increment/pre-gate toward CP-N4-A and reserve PASS/promotion language for S43.

findings.summary: A section titled FastAPI never constructs a FastAPI app, Pydantic model, Depends dependency, TestClient or generated OpenAPI contract in Theory.
findings.evidence: All nine theory executables are stdlib functions/dicts/lists.
findings.attack: Learner can finish Theory without encountering the actual framework semantics named in title and outcomes.
findings.defense: Stdlib models can isolate concepts before framework syntax.
findings.fix: Keep pure models as pre-step, then add a minimal real FastAPI/Pydantic/TestClient artifact for each boundary contract.

findings.summary: Theory playground for legacy id llm-finetuning still teaches simulated QLoRA/fine-tuning.
findings.evidence: SectionView mapping title is 'Practica QLoRA concepts (simulado)'.
findings.attack: The learner leaves HTTP contracts and is dropped into quantization/LoRA mathematics with zero transfer relation.
findings.defense: The stable legacy id itself is valid for progress compatibility.
findings.fix: Preserve id; replace only its playground mapping with an on-topic HTTP/idempotency/422/compatibility activity.

findings.summary: status_for returns 405 for unknown paths and emits no Allow contract for method-not-allowed responses.
findings.evidence: CE01: GET /v1/nope -> 405 while prose itself distinguishes unknown path 404 from known-path 405.
findings.attack: The executable contradicts both HTTP semantics and its own prose.
findings.defense: The toy only enumerates a few known routes.
findings.fix: Resolve path existence first, then method; return 404 for unknown resource and 405 plus allowed methods for known resource.

findings.summary: 201 creation is taught while Location is treated as merely optional rather than teaching the standard recommendation/representation relationship.
findings.evidence: T1-A says 'opcionalmente header Location'.
findings.attack: Learner misses an important part of discoverable create semantics.
findings.defense: A 201 response body can identify the created resource and Location is not universally mandatory.
findings.fix: State that 201 is the create status and Location is recommended when the new resource has a URI; test it in the real FastAPI response.

findings.summary: T1-B prose requires durable scoped atomic idempotency, but canonical code is a process-local dict with check-then-set.
findings.evidence: replay_label(store,key,body) performs if key in store then store[key]=body.
findings.attack: Concurrent requests and restarts can duplicate effects; this repeats unresolved S38 failure windows.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly warns that the sequential lab does not prove concurrency.
findings.fix: Use SQLite/transactional unique claim or equivalent durable store and test two concurrent requests plus process reopen.

findings.summary: The store retains a mutable body object rather than an immutable canonical fingerprint and stored response.
findings.evidence: CE06 mutating the caller's dict changes the stored comparison and turns a changed request into replay.
findings.attack: The idempotency record does not preserve original intent.
findings.defense: Simple dict equality demonstrates the conceptual same/different branch.
findings.fix: Canonicalize/fingerprint an immutable request representation and store original response/status with the claim.

findings.summary: Prose says identity is tenant/client + operation + key, but code indexes only key and stores no side-effect/result identity.
findings.evidence: store[key] = body.
findings.attack: Same key across tenants/endpoints can collide or replay another operation.
findings.defense: Single synthetic client/end-point keeps nominal example small.
findings.fix: Represent scope explicitly and regression-test cross-tenant/cross-operation key reuse.

findings.summary: page_keyset accepts invalid sizes and silently treats unknown cursors as end-of-data.
findings.evidence: CE02-CE04: size 0 crashes, negative size produces a page, unknown cursor yields empty terminal page.
findings.attack: Malformed/stale cursor can hide data instead of returning a typed client error.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses valid size and known cursor.
findings.fix: Validate positive bounded page size; make cursor parse/lookup failure explicit 400/422 with stable error type.

findings.summary: Keyset cursor uses a raw ID without asserting uniqueness, immutable ordering, tie-break, filter/as-of snapshot or opaque integrity.
findings.evidence: CE05 duplicate IDs make continuation ambiguous; code relies on list.index(first occurrence).
findings.attack: Concurrent inserts/duplicates/filter changes can skip or repeat rows.
findings.defense: The fixture job IDs happen to be unique and sorted.
findings.fix: Declare ordered unique cursor tuple, immutable sort semantics and filter/as-of binding; encode/sign opaque cursor in the production bridge.

findings.summary: Idempotency-Key is presented as an industry header without clarifying that the IETF specification is still a draft rather than a finalized RFC.
findings.evidence: T1-B references Stripe/industry practice.
findings.attack: Learner may mistake widespread vendor convention for finalized core HTTP semantics.
findings.defense: Calling it an industry header is broadly fair and the behavior taught is common.
findings.fix: Label it an industry convention with an IETF draft and document the service-specific scope/fingerprint/retention policy.

findings.summary: '/v1 congela campos públicos' reduces compatibility to preserving field names and has no explicit evolution policy.
findings.evidence: T1-B and T4-B focus on job_id/status rename/removal.
findings.attack: Consumers can break through type/requiredness/enum/error/ordering/pagination/semantic/rate-limit changes without any field rename.
findings.defense: Stable fields are a useful beginner anchor.
findings.fix: Define compatibility matrix for additions, requiredness, types, enum evolution, errors, ordering/pagination and behavioral limits; run old-consumer tests.

findings.summary: domain_imports_http=False is printed as a mental flag rather than proven by dependency direction/contract tests.
findings.evidence: routing_deps_models.py prints the literal False after two list-backed calls.
findings.attack: A real domain module could import FastAPI and the gate would still print False.
findings.defense: Injecting get_store does demonstrate substitutability at a toy scale.
findings.fix: Separate modules/interfaces and enforce import/port rules plus fake/adapter contract tests.

findings.summary: create_job derives job identity from len(store)+1.
findings.evidence: job id is f'job-{len(store)+1}'.
findings.attack: Deletion, concurrent writers or multiple stores can generate duplicate IDs; the API identity contract is not stable.
findings.defense: It is a tiny deterministic fixture.
findings.fix: Use a supplied stable synthetic ID/UUID-like generator and test uniqueness independently of collection length.

findings.summary: T2-B promises field types and ranges but executable validates only key presence.
findings.evidence: CE07 wrong types return 200.
findings.attack: A core FastAPI/Pydantic learning outcome false-greens malformed data.
findings.defense: Required-field presence is one legitimate validation layer.
findings.fix: Use a real Pydantic model with types/ranges/extra policy and assert 422 through TestClient.

findings.summary: OpenAPI alignment is narrated but no OpenAPI schema is generated or compared to runtime responses.
findings.evidence: public_view/reject_if_invalid are hand-written dict functions only.
findings.attack: Code and docs can drift while all S41 Theory examples stay green.
findings.defense: Allow-list serialization communicates the public/private distinction.
findings.fix: Use response_model/status declarations and assert paths/status/schema in app.openapi() plus TestClient responses.

findings.summary: Prose requires invalid input not call create_job, but the validator executable is not wired to the domain and cannot demonstrate zero side effects.
findings.evidence: reject_if_invalid returns tuples and never invokes create_job on either path.
findings.attack: A real handler could validate after mutating and still satisfy this disconnected demo.
findings.defense: Separation keeps validation concept simple.
findings.fix: Integrate validator + domain fake and assert store unchanged on 422.

findings.summary: Canonical work_boundary('durable') returns sync although the paragraph says durable work must leave request and be durably queued.
findings.evidence: CE08.
findings.attack: The code teaches the opposite routing for the explicit durable case.
findings.defense: Demo later has a slightly different mapping, showing author intent.
findings.fix: Represent CPU isolation and durability as independent dimensions; durable always requires durable enqueue before response.

findings.summary: The only queue is a process-local Python list.
findings.evidence: q=[]; queue.append({'id':..., 'status':'queued'}).
findings.attack: Restart loses work, directly violating the paragraph's durability requirement and inherited S38 recovery contract.
findings.defense: List makes the state transition visible without infrastructure.
findings.fix: Use local SQLite/outbox/queue fixture that survives reopen; keep list only as explicitly non-durable counterexample.

findings.summary: One string 'background' stands for both CPU isolation and durable job execution even though the prose correctly distinguishes the guarantees.
findings.evidence: work_boundary returns background for cpu_heavy and demo maps durable/background together.
findings.attack: Learner can conflate FastAPI BackgroundTasks, process pools and external durable workers.
findings.defense: The paragraph explicitly distinguishes them.
findings.fix: Return separate fields such as execution={inline_async, process_pool} and durability={request_scoped,durable_queue}.

findings.summary: trace_id is presented inside the RFC 9457 standard member list rather than as an extension.
findings.evidence: Paragraph says 'RFC 9457 Problem Details: type, title, status, trace_id'.
findings.attack: Learner mislearns the standardized Problem Details schema.
findings.defense: RFC 9457 permits extension members such as trace identifiers.
findings.fix: Teach standard members type/title/status/detail/instance and label trace_id as a service extension.

findings.summary: The lesson never teaches/asserts application/problem+json and omits detail/instance from the practical contract.
findings.evidence: problem_details returns only type/title/status/trace_id.
findings.attack: Learner may think any JSON dict with those fields is the wire-level RFC contract.
findings.defense: detail and instance are optional; minimal examples need not include every member.
findings.fix: Declare media type and distinguish optional standard members from extensions; add one real FastAPI exception response.

findings.summary: within_budget compares two numbers; it does not enforce a timeout or cancel work.
findings.evidence: No async wait, socket/future, deadline or cancellation appears in Theory.
findings.attack: 'timeout' can be printed without any operation having waited or been interrupted.
findings.defense: Numeric policy helper is useful for teaching budget order.
findings.fix: Use a local async slow coroutine/TestClient upstream fake and assert elapsed timeout/cancellation.

findings.summary: Resource lifecycle is represented by printing ['startup','shutdown']; no pool/resource is opened or closed.
findings.evidence: errors_timeouts_lifecycle.py contains no resource object/lifespan context.
findings.attack: The outcome can green without proving cleanup on normal or timeout paths.
findings.defense: The paragraph explains intended lifecycle correctly.
findings.fix: Use FastAPI lifespan or a closable fake and assert exactly-once open/close around TestClient lifecycle.

findings.summary: Timeout/cascade helpers accept impossible negative/non-finite budgets as valid evidence.
findings.evidence: CE09-CE10.
findings.attack: Corrupt monitoring/configuration can produce 'ok' or cascade=True.
findings.defense: Nominal examples use positive values.
findings.fix: Require finite positive durations and explicit headroom/deadline semantics before evaluating order.

findings.summary: level_detects is a hard-coded mapping of bug names to test layers, not a seeded bug caught by tests.
findings.evidence: Function returns booleans from two string comparisons.
findings.attack: No code defect is ever introduced or detected.
findings.defense: The mapping communicates conceptual ownership of test layers.
findings.fix: Seed actual domain/status/adapter faults and run unit/TestClient/integration tests that fail for the expected reason.

findings.summary: unit>=contract>=integration is taught as shape_ok, turning a heuristic into a numeric quality gate.
findings.evidence: pyramid_counts and callout explicitly use the inequality; CE11 negative counts still pass.
findings.attack: Teams can game counts while missing critical contracts; architecture/risk should drive test mix.
findings.defense: A broad base of cheaper tests is a useful heuristic.
findings.fix: Present pyramid as cost/feedback heuristic, validate nonnegative counts, and gate on required behaviors rather than count inequality.

findings.summary: T4-A promises unit/contract/integration but canonical detector only handles domain->unit and http->contract.
findings.evidence: level_detects has no adapter/integration branch in Theory code.
findings.attack: The third layer exists only in a count set, not in executable behavior.
findings.defense: The paragraph names a temp/in-memory adapter conceptually.
findings.fix: Add a controlled adapter/SQLite integration fault and an actual integration assertion.

findings.summary: S41 still has no collected pytest/FastAPI TestClient gate despite systematic pytest being mandatory since S27.
findings.evidence: Theory snippets print values; no tests collect endpoint behavior/OpenAPI/idempotency/restart/privacy regressions.
findings.attack: Critical API-contract regressions cannot block CI.
findings.defense: Print-based examples can remain useful for first exposure.
findings.fix: Promote nominal/edge/error cases into pytest + TestClient contract tests and preserve pure unit tests underneath.

findings.summary: Compatibility evidence is only a printed X-API-Version string and prose; no old consumer is run against a candidate response.
findings.evidence: T4-B prints compat_header only.
findings.attack: A breaking v1 response can still print the header and pass.
findings.defense: Stable job_id/status names are a reasonable anchor.
findings.fix: Freeze a v1 consumer/schema fixture and run it against candidate API responses/OpenAPI.

findings.summary: Read compatibility is framed mainly as preserving job_id/status fields.
findings.evidence: T4-B wording focuses on rename/remove.
findings.attack: Required fields, types, enum values, errors, semantics, ordering/pagination and rate-limit behavior can all break consumers.
findings.defense: Field preservation is the simplest visible example.
findings.fix: Teach additive-change rules and explicit compatibility policy across schema, semantics and operational contracts.

findings.summary: rate_decision compares supplied used/limit values but has no clock/window, client scope, mutable claim, refill or concurrency safety.
findings.evidence: Function is a pure if used>limit.
findings.attack: It cannot prove requests per time window or protect a service under concurrent clients, repeating S38's static-quota defect.
findings.defense: It illustrates allow vs 429 decision shape.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic fake clock/window and client key, atomic counter/token bucket, and test rollover/concurrency.

findings.summary: Negative/NaN usage and invalid limits can allow traffic or manufacture impossible remaining quota.
findings.evidence: CE12-CE13.
findings.attack: Corrupt quota telemetry fails open.
findings.defense: Nominal fixture uses integers 73/100 and 110/100.
findings.fix: Validate finite nonnegative integer counts and positive policy limits before decision.

findings.summary: 429 returns a JSON retry_after_s member but no Retry-After response header or explicit time-window semantics.
findings.evidence: rate_decision output contains retry_after_s:1 only.
findings.attack: Client interoperability is taught as body convention rather than HTTP response contract.
findings.defense: RFC 6585 makes Retry-After optional, not mandatory.
findings.fix: Teach/use Retry-After when the service knows the retry time and bind it to the limiter window.

findings.summary: trace_safe checks only exact top-level field names against a small ban list.
findings.evidence: CE14-CE15 pass PII embedded in values or differently cased keys.
findings.attack: Logs/traces can leak email/DNI/secret while trace_ok=True.
findings.defense: Allow/deny field-name examples can introduce minimization.
findings.fix: Use an allowlisted structured telemetry schema with nested validation/redaction and tests containing adversarial PII values/aliases.

findings.summary: The lesson treats a trace_id string as observability evidence without spans/span_id/propagation across request->job->result.
findings.evidence: T4-B only passes {'trace_id','job_id'} to trace_safe.
findings.attack: A random identifier cannot show parent/child timing or cross-boundary trace continuity.
findings.defense: Correlation identifiers are useful first observability primitives.
findings.fix: Model at least trace_id + span_id + propagation into durable job context and one child span/result.

findings.summary: Tagline/gate promise no PII or internal keys across API evidence, but only one hand-picked response allow-list and top-level trace ban list are checked.
findings.evidence: Errors, OpenAPI examples, headers, nested payloads and trace attributes are not machine-validated.
findings.attack: The service can leak secrets outside the single public_view example while still passing all printed flags.
findings.defense: The section consistently advocates minimization in prose.
findings.fix: Define shared public/error/log/trace schemas and run leakage regression tests over all response and telemetry surfaces.

findings.summary: Dense English/API jargon appears faster than self-contained Spanish explanations in an already advanced transition section.
findings.evidence: path operation, body, keyset, boundary, background, shape, allow-list, rate limit, trace, lifecycle, replay, handler appear densely.
findings.attack: Learners can memorize tokens without a causal model of trigger/input/action/result.
findings.defense: Many are actual framework/industry terms and should remain recognizable.
findings.fix: Define each once Spanish-first, retain the API term in parentheses/code, then reuse consistently.

findings.summary: T1-A states resources should use nouns and not verbs with protocol-like certainty.
findings.evidence: 'Modela recursos con sustantivos versionados ... no verbos en la URL.'
findings.attack: This is a useful REST-style design convention, not an HTTP correctness requirement; RPC/action endpoints can be legitimate.
findings.defense: Resource-oriented noun paths are a strong default for the course's API design.
findings.fix: Label noun-oriented paths as this service's resource-style convention and distinguish protocol semantics from house style.

USABLE: HTTP status is part of the public contract; collection-empty is not item-not-found.
Sequential replay with the same logical idempotency identity should not create a second side effect.
Same idempotency identity with a different payload should fail as a conflict rather than silently mutate intent.
Keyset pagination can be preferable to offset when backed by a stable unique ordering contract.
Handlers should orchestrate and domain logic should not depend on framework HTTP objects.
Public response schemas should be minimized/allowlisted.
I/O async, CPU isolation and durable background execution are distinct concerns.
Problem Details is a stable machine-readable error pattern and can carry service-specific extension members.
Rate-limit rejection should use HTTP 429 rather than an opaque 500.
Compatibility must be tested against consumers rather than inferred from version labels alone.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: S41 local asserts equal CP-N4-A promotion even though CP-N4-A gate is S43
